question:
For $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 0\\1 & 2 & 1\\0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$:

(a) Find $|A|$ and $\operatorname{adj}A$.

(b) Hence, determine $A^{-1}$.

(c) Verify the inverse by calculating $A(\operatorname{adj}A)$ and comparing it with $|A|I$.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 2\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\0 & 2\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=2(4-1)-(2-0)=6-2=4$$
The cofactor matrix is
$$C=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & 1\\-2 & 4 & -2\\1 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
Since this matrix is symmetric,
$$\operatorname{adj}A=C^T=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & 1\\-2 & 4 & -2\\1 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
Since $|A|=4\neq0$,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & 1\\-2 & 4 & -2\\1 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$

(c)
Multiplying $A$ by its adjoint,
$$A(\operatorname{adj}A)=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 0\\1 & 2 & 1\\0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & 1\\-2 & 4 & -2\\1 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0\\0 & 4 & 0\\0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}=4I=|A|I$$
Therefore, $A^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{adj}A$ is verified.
